newsitem.title: UK: Labour's first 100 days get okay from managers.
newsitem.headline: Labour's first 100 days get okay from managers.

text.p: Britain's managers gave the Labour government a score of six out of ten for its first 100 days in office, according to a poll by the Institute of Management (IM) released on Friday.

Prime Minister Tony Blair scored seven out of ten for his leadership skills, while the government as a whole was awarded sixes for its performance in Europe, its partnership with business and its ability to do the job.
"Labour's first term has been one of steady progress," said IM director general Roger Young.
"Labour in office has been as good as its word and delivered on many of the policies business leaders were looking for. While gold stars may be absent from the report card, the silvers are solid,"

Around 70 percent of the 316 managers polled said Labour had demonstrated a more open style of government and a willingness to consult, while 50 percent believed the Labour government was in touch with the real needs of business.

More than four in ten managers said they believed Labour had a clear strategy for the economy, but 70 percent said the Chancellor's decision not to raise personal taxes in his first budget last month was driven more by politics than the need to manage the economy prudently.
Approval for Labour's approach to Europe was strong, with 79 percent of managers saying Britain's relationship with Europe had improved under Labour.

Sixty-two percent said Britain should join a single European currency if the convergence criteria were met and 58 percent said they believed a single currency would affect their organisations whether Britain joined or not.
Over half those surveyed said their organisations had not started planning for a single currency and 70 percent said they did not believe it would start in 1999.
